title: Keeping a Way to Change Your Mind
one_sentence_thesis: A resolution does not automatically justify refusing maintenance of the arrangements supporting it, and a recognized shortfall in that support can call for informational repair while the project remains settled.
contribution: A diagnostic account of misapplying a reason against project reconsideration to the conditions supporting that reason; it distinguishes sufficient surviving grounds, recognized insufficiency, reasonable doubt, policy permissibility, actual reasoning, and repair of a missed informational interval.
strongest_objection: The strongest existing combination of planning theory, ordinary instrumental reasoning and defeater responsiveness may already explain the same recommendations; the remaining contribution is the structure and corrective target of a specific justificatory mistake.
originality_limitations: No comprehensive originality search. Holton already permits monitoring and implementation, Anaya develops strategies of defeater responsiveness, and rationale-based monitoring is established technical work. The final claims diagnostic clarification, not a new fundamental norm or an independently created repair duty.
open_questions: Does making the justificatory inference explicit add enough explanatory value beyond familiar accounts?
How should sufficient practical support and reasonable doubt be assessed across purposes and risk tolerances?
When can retrospective informational repair remain distinct from project reconsideration?
Which psychologically feasible arrangements combine usable warnings with resistance to temptation?
